# Go Backend Agent Rules (`AGENTS-go.md`)

> **To use:** copy the full content of `AGENTS-backend.md` into your project's `AGENTS.md`, then append the content of this file below it. The combined file becomes your project's `AGENTS.md`.
> Go-specific rules. Extends the universal backend baseline — all rules in `AGENTS-backend.md` remain in force. This file adds only Go-specific invariants.

## 1. Go Idioms & Error Handling

- [ ] **Wrap at Package Boundaries**: Every error returned from an external package or cross-layer call MUST be wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("operation context: %w", err)` to preserve the error chain while adding call-site context.
- [ ] **Inspect with `errors.Is` / `errors.As`**: Callers MUST use `errors.Is` for sentinel comparison and `errors.As` for typed unwrapping; direct `==` equality on error values is banned.
- [ ] **Never Ignore Errors**: The blank identifier `_` MUST NOT be used to discard error return values. Every error must be explicitly checked, wrapped, or returned.
- [ ] **Guard Clauses Over Nesting**: Error branches MUST exit early (`return`, `continue`, or `break`), keeping the happy path at the left margin. `else` blocks after an error-returning `if` are banned.
- [ ] **Log OR Return, Not Both**: An error MUST be either logged at the point of final handling or returned to the caller — never both. Double-logging creates duplicate noise and obscures the true failure site.
- [ ] **`panic` Banned in Library Code**: `panic` is reserved for truly unrecoverable programmer errors in `main` or initialisation; it MUST NOT appear in reusable packages, service, or repository layers.

## 2. Module System & Toolchain

- [ ] **Toolchain Directive**: `go.mod` MUST contain a `toolchain go1.X.Y` directive (version ≥ the `go` directive) to declare the preferred toolchain. This is a preference, not a hard lock — CI MUST also pin `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.X.Y` (exact version string) for full build reproducibility. Note: `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` allows auto-download when the installed version is older than the directive; `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` restricts to the pre-installed toolchain and is the recommended CI setting; `GOTOOLCHAIN=off` is more aggressive and disables toolchain-switching entirely.
- [ ] **Readonly Builds in CI**: CI MUST set `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly` to prevent the Go toolchain from silently modifying `go.mod` or `go.sum` during builds — without this flag, a build can pass on a dirty module state, defeating the pre-commit `go mod tidy` gate.
- [ ] **`go.sum` Committed and Verified**: `go.sum` MUST be committed to version control and `go mod verify` MUST be run in CI as a belt-and-suspenders step. Note: the Go toolchain already verifies checksums on download; for stronger supply-chain assurance also consider SBOM generation.
- [ ] **`go mod tidy` Before Commit**: `go mod tidy` MUST be run before committing to ensure `go.mod` and `go.sum` reflect exactly the packages imported by the source — no phantom or missing entries.
- [ ] **No `replace` Directives in Main Branch**: `replace` directives used for local development MUST be removed before merging. Committed `replace` directives break builds for all other consumers.
- [ ] **`go vet` Clean**: `go vet ./...` MUST produce zero diagnostics in CI; vet failures are treated as build failures.
- [ ] **`golangci-lint` Gate**: CI MUST run `golangci-lint run` with at minimum `errcheck`, `staticcheck`, `gosec`, `revive`, and `sloglint` enabled in `.golangci.yml`; any issue exits non-zero and blocks merge. Configure `sloglint` with `no-global: "default"` — this flags all top-level `slog.*` convenience functions (e.g., `slog.Info`, `slog.Error`) that implicitly use the default logger, while permitting custom package-level `*slog.Logger` variables. Do NOT use `no-global: "all"` as it additionally bans custom package-level logger variables, conflicting with the `slog.SetDefault` pattern required in §5. (Note: `deadcode`, `structcheck`, and `varcheck` were removed in recent golangci-lint versions and are superseded by `staticcheck`; do not re-add them.)
- [ ] **`govulncheck` Gate**: CI MUST run `govulncheck ./...`; any confirmed reachable vulnerability in a dependency blocks merge until the dependency is patched or the finding is explicitly accepted with a written justification.

## 3. Concurrency & Goroutine Hygiene

- [ ] **Context Propagation into Every Goroutine**: Every goroutine that performs I/O or blocking work MUST receive a `context.Context` as its first argument and MUST `select` on `<-ctx.Done()` to exit gracefully on cancellation.
- [ ] **`defer cancel()` Immediately After Creation**: The `cancel` function returned by `context.WithCancel` or `context.WithTimeout` MUST be deferred on the very next line of its declaration to prevent context leaks regardless of the execution path.
- [ ] **`sync.WaitGroup` Discipline**: Every `wg.Add(1)` call MUST have exactly one corresponding `defer wg.Done()` inside the spawned goroutine; `Add` MUST be called in the parent goroutine before the `go` statement.
- [ ] **No Unbounded Goroutine Spawning**: Goroutines MUST NOT be spawned one-per-request or one-per-item on unbounded dynamic inputs. Use fixed-size worker pools (buffered channel semaphore or `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` with `SetLimit`) to cap concurrency.
- [ ] **Goroutine Leak Detection in Tests**: Test suites MUST import `go.uber.org/goleak` and call `goleak.VerifyTestMain(m)` in `TestMain` as the primary leak detection mechanism — it is the recommended default. `defer goleak.VerifyNone(t)` MUST NOT be used in any package where any test file calls `t.Parallel()` — a single parallel test anywhere in the package causes `VerifyNone` to produce false positives from sibling goroutines still running at sample time.
- [ ] **Goroutine Count Metric**: Services MUST export `runtime.NumGoroutine()` as a gauge metric and alert operations when it grows monotonically, indicating a leak in production before an OOM event occurs.

## 4. HTTP & Router Patterns

- [ ] **Thin Handler Rule**: HTTP handlers MUST only validate the incoming request, delegate to a service method, and encode the response. Business logic, database access, and error mapping MUST NOT appear directly in handler bodies.
- [ ] **Dependency Injection via Handler Structs**: Dependencies (service interfaces, logger, config) MUST be injected into a handler struct at wiring time. Package-level variables and `init()`-based globals for dependencies are banned.
- [ ] **Router Selection**: Use `go-chi/chi` for complex APIs requiring middleware groups and nested routing, or the standard `net/http` `ServeMux` for simpler services. Note: method + path pattern matching on `net/http.ServeMux` requires Go 1.22+; projects targeting an older `go` directive MUST use `go-chi/chi`.
- [ ] **Explicit `http.Server` Timeouts**: Every `http.Server` instance MUST set `ReadTimeout`, `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, and `IdleTimeout`; omitting any timeout leaves the server vulnerable to slow-client and Slowloris attacks and resource exhaustion.
- [ ] **Recovery & Request-ID Middleware**: `middleware.Recoverer` (imported from `github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware`, or a semantically identical recovery middleware if chi is not used) MUST be applied globally to convert panics into 500 responses without crashing the process; `middleware.RequestID` MUST inject a unique request ID into every request context and log line.
- [ ] **Input Validation at Route Boundary**: Handler code MUST decode and validate request bodies and path/query parameters before calling service methods, returning structured `400 Bad Request` responses for undeclared or invalid fields — this is the Go-layer mechanism for the backend baseline's strict schema validation invariant.
- [ ] **Graceful HTTP Shutdown**: Services MUST listen for `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` using `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)` (Go 1.16+). On signal receipt: (1) call `stop()` (the cancel function returned by `signal.NotifyContext`) immediately to restore default signal behaviour so a second signal can force-kill during the drain window; (2) create a new shutdown context with `shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)` and `defer cancel()` immediately to prevent a context leak; (3) call `srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)` — NOT the already-cancelled signal context, which would cause `Shutdown` to return immediately and drop in-flight requests. See also `AGENTS-backend.md §5` (Kubernetes Drain Coordination) for required preStop lifecycle hook configuration.

## 5. Observability & Logging with `log/slog`

- [ ] **`slog.JSONHandler` in Production**: The default logger MUST be initialised in `main()` using `slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stdout, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelInfo}))` and registered via `slog.SetDefault` so all package-level `slog.*` calls emit machine-parseable JSON.
- [ ] **Request-Scoped Logger with `slog.With`**: HTTP middleware MUST derive a per-request logger with `slog.With("trace_id", traceID, "request_id", requestID)` and store it in the request context; downstream handlers and service calls MUST retrieve it from context — this is the Go mechanism for the backend baseline's trace_id-on-every-log invariant.
- [ ] **OTel Trace ID Binding**: The `trace_id` value injected into each request logger MUST be extracted from the active OpenTelemetry span and guarded for validity: `spanCtx := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx).SpanContext(); if spanCtx.IsValid() { traceID = spanCtx.TraceID().String() }`. The `IsValid()` guard is required — without it, un-instrumented code paths silently log an all-zeros trace ID, polluting distributed trace correlation.
- [ ] **`slog.Any("error", err)` for Errors**: Error log entries MUST pass the error value as a structured attribute using `slog.Any("error", err)`; embedding errors in the message string is banned because it discards `%w`-wrapped chain context. Define a package-level helper `func Err(err error) slog.Attr { return slog.Any("error", err) }` to enforce key consistency and prevent `"err"` / `"error"` key drift across the codebase.
- [ ] **No Secrets or PII in Logs**: Log calls MUST NOT include passwords, tokens, API keys, full card numbers, or personally identifiable information. Sensitive data MUST be wrapped in a named type (e.g., `type APIKey string`) that implements `slog.LogValuer` — defining `LogValue() slog.Value` to return a redacted placeholder — so the default `slog` formatter never emits the raw value. Note: `sloglint` enforces consistent call structure; PII protection relies on the `slog.LogValuer` pattern, not on `sloglint`.
- [ ] **`pprof` on Dedicated Internal Mux**: pprof handlers MUST be registered explicitly on a **dedicated `http.NewServeMux()`** (not `http.DefaultServeMux`) bound to `localhost:6060`, and a separate `http.Server` MUST be started on an internal-only goroutine for that mux. The blank import `_ "net/http/pprof"` pattern MUST NOT be used — it pollutes the global default mux and risks exposing debug endpoints on the public-facing port if anything else uses `http.DefaultServeMux`.

## 6. Testing & Tooling Baseline

- [ ] **Table-Driven Tests with `t.Run`**: All unit tests covering multiple input variants MUST use the table-driven pattern — a slice of named structs iterated with `t.Run(tt.name, ...)` — so individual cases are independently runnable and clearly identified in failure output.
- [ ] **Race Detector in CI**: CI MUST run `go test -race ./...`; any data race detected by the race detector is a blocking failure equivalent to a test failure.
- [ ] **`testify` for Assertions and Mocks**: Tests MUST use `github.com/stretchr/testify/assert` (non-fatal assertions) and `github.com/stretchr/testify/require` (fatal precondition checks) for readable failure messages. Interface mocks MUST use either `testify/mock` (handwritten or `mockery`-generated) OR `go.uber.org/mock` (the actively maintained successor to the deprecated `github.com/golang/mock`, with controller-based verification) — both paradigms MUST NOT be mixed within a single package. Teams migrating from `github.com/golang/mock` MUST also update the code generator: `go install go.uber.org/mock/mockgen@latest`.
- [ ] **Containerized Integration Tests**: Integration tests touching a real database or message broker MUST use `github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go` to spin up ephemeral containers — this is the Go mechanism for the backend baseline's Testcontainers integration test invariant.
- [ ] **No Shared Mutable State Between Tests**: Tests MUST NOT share package-level mutable variables, open file handles, or database connections across test functions; each test MUST set up and tear down its own state to ensure isolation regardless of execution order or `-parallel` flag.
- [ ] **Full CI Gate**: The CI pipeline MUST run `go build ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, and `govulncheck ./...` as sequential gates — all must pass before a PR is eligible for merge.
- [ ] **Contract Diff & Authorization Tests**: Implement the backend baseline's OpenAPI/Proto contract diff gate using `oasdiff` (`github.com/oasdiff/oasdiff`, Go-native, OpenAPI 3.x) for REST or `buf breaking` for Protobuf contracts. For OpenAPI 3.1 code generation use `oapi-codegen` (`github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen/v2`) or `ogen`. Note: `go-swagger` targets OpenAPI 2.0 only and MUST NOT be used for OpenAPI 3.1 projects. Every protected resource MUST have at least one table-driven negative authorization test asserting that a valid but unauthorized principal receives `403 Forbidden` — not the resource data.

## 7. Resilience (Go-Specific Mechanisms)

- [ ] **HTTP Client Timeouts**: Every `http.Client` used for outgoing requests MUST set an explicit `Timeout` field — the zero value results in no timeout, leaving the service vulnerable to slow or hung upstream dependencies. There is no global default.
- [ ] **Database Driver Timeouts**: Database drivers MUST configure explicit connection and query timeouts via their DSN parameters or connection pool configuration (e.g., `connect_timeout`, `statement_timeout` for `pgx`/`lib/pq`); never rely on driver defaults.
- [ ] **Circuit Breakers on Non-Critical Dependencies**: Non-critical external integrations MUST be wrapped in a circuit breaker per the backend baseline. Use `github.com/sony/gobreaker/v2` (Go-generics API) or `github.com/failsafe-go/failsafe-go` for Go-idiomatic circuit breaker and retry-with-jitter implementations.
